# 孔雀王呪經

**Dynasty:** 梁

## Contributors

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Liáng-period (Southern dynasties) translation of the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyā* by **Saṅghapāla** ([僧伽婆羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85)) — the Funan-born *trepiṭaka* who served the Liáng emperor Wǔdì at the *Shòuguāngdiàn* 壽光殿 imperial translation bureau in Jiànkāng. The text is one of the earliest *Mahāmāyūrī* recensions in the Chinese canon (alongside Kumārajīva's T988, [KR6j0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0175)) and predates Yìjìng's later seventh-century retranslation ([KR6j0172](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0172)) and Amoghavajra's eighth-century definitive recension ([KR6j0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0167)).

**Abstract**

Saṅghapāla (僧伽婆羅, ca. 460–524, Skt. Saṅghapāla / Saṅghavarman) was a Funan (扶南, Mekong delta) Buddhist monk who arrived at the Liáng capital ca. 503 and was assigned by emperor Wǔdì to lead the imperial translation bureau. His translation activity is documented in the *Liáng gāosēng zhuàn* 梁高僧傳 ([KR6r0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0052)) by [慧皎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E7%9A%8E) Huìjiǎo and in [僧祐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E7%A5%90) Sēngyòu's *Chū sānzàng jì jí* 出三藏記集 ([KR6s0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084)). The *Kǒngquè wáng zhòu jīng* gives the standard early-medieval *Mahāmāyūrī* recension with the Svāti narrative *nidāna*, the principal *vidyā*, and an early form of the *yakṣa*-general geographical list — though substantially shorter than Amoghavajra's expanded T982 list. Saṅghapāla's translation enjoyed wide circulation in the Liáng-Chén-Sui and early-Tang periods before being progressively superseded by the later recensions; it remains valuable as a witness to the early-medieval Indic recensional history of the *Mahāmāyūrī*.
